messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident declared — GPU containers in eu-west-1a are restarting repeatedly. Symptom: OOM during prefill for large-context requests. Pager sent to @alice-oncall and @erin-pager.

alice-oncall: I'm on it. Acknowledged. Pinging SRE/runtime.

bob-sre: grabbing logs. Seeing repeated SIGKILL and 'out of memory' from the prefill stage (long prompts). Restart count +120 in last 5m for pool rwd-eu-west-1a/gpu-ml-1.

carol-runtime: adding context — model variants serving long-window requests with kv-cache spikes. Prefill token distribution shows a heavy tail (requests > 64k tokens). Runtime prefill isn't trimming.

frank-infra: nodes look healthy aside from oom restarts. NVidia driver resets? No, driver is OK. Container OOM only.

alice-oncall: Customer impact? Any 5xxs or increase in latency surfaced to API users?

grace-observability: API 5xxs up ~2.1% in eu-west-1a, error graph: container_restart_count spike correlates with prefill throughput. Embedding generation for some customers dropped.

erin-pager: I've paged the rotation team. Suggest immediate mitigation: enforce per-request prefill cap + route large-context requests to fallback pool (cpu or low-memory model) until patched.

bob-sre: quick mitigation steps I can run now: 1) Set prefill_max_tokens=8192 globally for the pool 2) Enable aggressive prefill_kv_eviction for long sessions 3) Scale up pool with spare nodes. Which do you want first?

alice-oncall: Do #1 and #2. Scaling is slower — start config changes first. Keep me posted.

carol-runtime: Applying hot-config:
```
redwoodctl runtime set-config --pool rwd-eu-west-1a/gpu-ml-1 \
  --prefill_max_tokens=8192 \
  --prefill_kv_eviction=aggressive
```
I will roll to 20% canary, then 100% if stable.

frank-infra: I'll reserve 2 spare nodes and start a node rotation; will cordon two highest-oom hosts.

alice-oncall: Erin, prep a short customer-impact note with ETA for mitigation. Dave — can you draft customer-facing language?

dave-cs: Drafting now. Short note: "We are mitigating an infrastructure issue causing intermittent generation errors for some long-context requests in EU-West. We're rolling a configuration fix; no data loss. We will follow up with full incident report." Want to add any SLA/credits language?

erin-pager: Send that. ETA for full mitigation ~15–25m after canary passes. I'll update status page and the incident ticket.

bob-sre: Canary rolled — initial 20% rolled. No new restarts in canary for 3m. Increasing to 100% now.

carol-runtime: 100% roll complete. Metrics look better: container_restarts down to baseline in canary cluster. Observability, can you confirm global?

grace-observability: Confirmed: restarts trend down ~95% in 10m. 5xxs trending back to prior baseline. Prefill token spike suppressed.

frank-infra: Node rotation in progress. Cordoned hosts drained without additional restarts.

alice-oncall: Great. Immediate mitigation successful. Assigning follow-ups:
- Postmortem owner: @bob-sre
- Runtime change: add automatic prefill trimming for >32k tokens: @carol-runtime
- Observability: add prefill token histograms alerting >10 requests/min at >16k tokens: @grace-observability
- Customer comms: finalize update and schedule follow-up: @dave-cs

bob-sre: Taking postmortem. Initial hypothesis: unbounded long-context prefill + KV cache growth + insufficient eviction policy caused per-container OOM cascade under high concurrency.

carol-runtime: I'll prototype an automatic prefill stream-trim and a guardrail that rejects >64k tokens with explicit 413-like error to avoid silent OOMs.

erin-pager: Closing pager for now. I'll reopen if symptoms reappear.

dave-cs: Sent live update to affected customers. Keeping them posted.

alice-oncall: Thanks team. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and resolution. Moving to "mitigated" — still in progress for post-incident follow-ups. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to SEV3; follow-ups logged in INC-1924680000.

bob-sre: Final note — add a perf/regression test that synthesizes very long prefill sequences to run in staging; prevents future regressions.

carol-runtime: Agree. Will open RFC for long-context handling and default limits.

alice-oncall: Good work everyone. Stand down unless we see regressions.
